supersedes: v4 (WITHDRAWN, never governed any run) and v3 (governed the aborted batch of 2026-09-13T18:07Z). v3 is retained as S15_INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_V3.json and its data is archived under s15_aborted_20260913T182252Z/. v2 and v1 are retained as _SUPERSEDED copies.
why_v2_exists: v1 defined the receiver statistic as 'the maximum dispersion among servo samples recorded after the netem apply event'. The S14 development value was in fact a single summary window, not a maximum across several. A last summary and a maximum across several summaries are different measures, so v1 would have compared the detector against a statistic the boundary was never derived from. v2 uses one statistic for both: the dispersion of the FIRST valid wholly-in-phase summary window.

v1 did not state how a summary window is aligned to a phase. ptp4l summary windows are sample-count driven and a window that straddles the netem apply instant mixes two phases. v2 requires the whole window to lie inside the intended phase and declares a minimum window count.
v1 labels IMPACTED / NOT_IMPACTED read as harm claims. v2 uses RECEIVER_DISPERSION_ABOVE_BOUNDARY / BELOW_BOUNDARY, which name a measurement category only.

v1 ordered the five levels in fixed ascending sequence in every repetition, confounding level with position in the batch. v2 uses a counterbalanced randomised order fixed in advance from a recorded seed.
The impaired phase was lengthened from 50 s to 80 s so that at least two whole summary windows fall inside it.
purpose: Test whether the packet detector's run-level decision agrees with an independently computed, receiver-side measurement label across a graded jitter sweep including levels between the two S14 settings. The measurement label is produced by ptp4l's servo, not by the detector.
development_exclusion: The receiver statistic and its boundary were derived from S14 data. S14, S11, S12 and all V1-V5 runs are development data and are excluded from S15 estimation. S15 runs are the independent test set and must not be used to retune anything.
not_claimed: S15 can establish only whether a packet-level decision agrees with a receiver-side path-delay dispersion measurement in this software testbed. It cannot establish harm, service impact, physical timing accuracy, attack detection, recovery benefit, or O-RAN conformance. Harmfulness remains UNKNOWN: no service requirement has been specified against which a path-delay dispersion could be judged harmful. S14's agreement between configured condition and measured dispersion is NOT validated harmful-versus-harmless classification.

frozen_rule.detector_note: Eight matched Sync/Follow_Up arrival-gap samples per block; two high, disjoint blocks within three seconds. Blocks need not be consecutive. 160 us is provisional engineering configuration, not a validated harm boundary.
frozen_rule.hash_note: Trial runner and evaluator hashes differ from v3 because of the corrections above, and apply_impairment.py is new. Every superseded artifact is preserved byte-identical under a _SUPERSEDED name with its hash recorded here. All edits were made before any S15 run existed.
frozen_rule.evaluator_note: evaluate_s15.py executes this protocol and contains no tunable parameter. Its boundary, minimum window count and ambiguity band are quoted from this file. Any edit to the evaluator after the first S15 run invalidates the validation.

topology: Two independent L2 bridges, one master per segment, one slaveOnly ptp4l with a port on each. Identical to S14. A run whose receiver enters MASTER on either port is recorded UNKNOWN.
host_clock_protection: ptp4l runs with free_running 1 on every instance. The host software clock is never disciplined and no host network outside the created namespaces is modified.
why_these_levels: Mean delay is held at 100 us in every arm so it cannot separate conditions; only configured jitter varies. j020 and j200 reproduce the two S14 settings; j060, j100 and j140 lie between them so the decision boundary is not pre-baked into the design.

trial_ordering.design: Counterbalanced and randomised, fixed before any run. Repetitions 1-5 are the rows of a 5x5 cyclic Latin square whose level labels and row order were randomly permuted; repetition 6 is one additional randomly permuted sequence.
trial_ordering.generator: python random.Random(20260913): shuffle level labels, build cyclic square, shuffle rows, then shuffle one extra repetition
trial_ordering.balance_note: Across repetitions 1-5 each level occupies each position exactly once. Repetition 6 adds one extra occurrence per level, so one position per level has count 2. Perfect balance is not attainable with six repetitions of five levels.
trial_ordering.binding: The same sequences are written literally into run_s15_validation_batch.sh, whose sha256 is recorded above. The script does not regenerate the order at run time.

phases.detector_lifetime_rule: DET_SETUP_MARGIN(20) + SETTLE(12) + IMPAIR(80) + DET_DRAIN_MARGIN(60). A bounded watchdog, not a schedule.
phases.impaired_length_reason: S14's impaired phase was 30 s and produced exactly one wholly-in-phase servo summary window per run, because ptp4l printed a summary about every 16.0 s under this configuration and the window straddling the apply instant is discarded. One window per run cannot satisfy the two-window minimum, so the S15 impaired phase is 80 s. At a 16 s cadence that yields about five printed summaries after the apply instant, of which about four lie wholly inside the phase. The lengthening was decided before any S15 run and affects only how many windows exist, not which window is used: the statistic remains the FIRST valid window.
phases.s14_cadence_evidence: 20260913_s14_jnoact1: ptp4l start 617.11, apply 629.35, summaries at 629.576 (first after start, invalid) and 645.597 (window 629.576-645.597, duration 16.021 s, valid). Phase ended 659.58 before a third summary was printed.

receiver_measurement.source: ptp4l receiver servo summary line in slave.log, field `delay <mean> +/- <dispersion>`, nanoseconds
receiver_measurement.semantics_provenance: linuxptp clock.c: clock_stats_update prints on sample count reaching max_count; clock_stats_display then calls stats_reset on offset, freq and delay. Window = (previous summary, this summary]. Units nanoseconds per ptp4l(8).
receiver_measurement.documentation_provenance: ptp4l(8) summary_interval: power of two in seconds, default 0 (1 second), units nanoseconds and ppb
receiver_measurement.statistic: The dispersion of the FIRST valid wholly-in-phase summary window of the impaired phase. This is the same statistic used on the S14 development data that produced the boundary.
receiver_measurement.why_not_a_maximum: A maximum over an unspecified number of windows depends on how many windows a run happens to produce, so it is not comparable between runs or between S14 and S15.
receiver_measurement.validity_rule: A summary window is valid only if it lies WHOLLY inside the declared impaired phase: window_start >= the apply upper bound AND window_end + 1 ms <= phase2_end_recorded AND window_end + 1 ms <= any port FAULTY transition. Window_start is the preceding printed summary's timestamp. The first summary after ptp4l start is always invalid.
receiver_measurement.insufficient_windows_rule: A run producing fewer than two valid wholly-in-phase windows is recorded UNKNOWN with reason insufficient_valid_windows. It is reported, never silently dropped.

phase_alignment.phase_clock: CLOCK_MONOTONIC read by python time.clock_gettime in the runner, recorded to 6 decimal places. Identical clock to linuxptp print.c and to the detector's time.monotonic().
phase_alignment.ptp4l_log_rounding: truncation, so a logged time is always <= the true time
phase_alignment.apply_instant: an interval [phase2_apply_begin, phase2_graded_jitter_applied_seg1], both timestamps taken inside apply_impairment.py immediately around the tc call. The interval is the width of the command, not of a shell round trip. Eligibility uses the later bound.
phase_alignment.eligibility_start: window_start_logged >= apply_upper_bound. Because a logged ptp4l time is <= the true time, this guarantees the true window start is at or after the true apply instant with no further allowance.
phase_alignment.eligibility_end: window_end_logged + 0.001 <= phase2_end_recorded, and likewise for any fault transition. This is the conservative form of 'ends before'.
phase_alignment.no_fixed_band: The superseded evaluator excluded windows starting within a fixed 1 ms of the apply instant. That band was finer than the 10 ms phase clock then in use and was derived from nothing recorded. It is deleted.
phase_alignment.legacy_fallback: A run recorded by a superseded runner has no begin timestamp; its apply upper bound is padded by the 10 ms phase-clock quantum and the run is flagged with apply_basis.
phase_alignment.empirical_cross_check_limitation: The anchor is a command and its direct effect, so the difference also contains the true command-to-fault latency. It bounds the clock offset from above; it does not prove a zero offset.
phase_alignment.empirical_cross_check_status: Corroboration only. The alignment claim now rests on the two clocks being the SAME clock, read by the same system call, which is verified in source rather than inferred from five anchors.

receiver_measurement.boundary_provenance: Midpoint of the S14 development separation under this same statistic: benign_delay_jitter maximum 24615 ns and jitter-fault minimum 33330 ns. Their midpoint is 28972.5 ns, rounded to 29000 ns for a readable frozen constant. The rounding moves the boundary 27.5 ns towards the fault side, which is 0.3 percent of the 8715 ns separation and cannot change any S14 development label. Derived from development data; S15 is its first independent test.
receiver_measurement.label_semantics: RECEIVER_DISPERSION_ABOVE_BOUNDARY / BELOW_BOUNDARY are names for a measurement category only. They are NOT harm labels, NOT fault labels and NOT service-impact labels. Harmfulness remains UNKNOWN.
receiver_measurement.independence_caveat: A separate receiver-computed channel, produced by ptp4l rather than the detector. NOT statistically independent of the packet observations: both arise from the same traffic.
unknown_rules: fewer than two valid wholly-in-phase windows
no valid wholly-in-phase window at all
receiver entered MASTER on either port
run unsealed or any manifest hash mismatch
receiver_measurement.containment_note: The impairment persists past phase2_end_recorded until teardown, so strict containment rejects some genuinely impaired windows. Rejecting is the conservative direction.

detector_decision.quantity: Per run: whether the live detector recorded a detection_trigger event attributable to the impaired phase. Nothing else.
detector_decision.observation_window_rule: A detection_trigger counts only if the packet timestamp that produced it (packet_ts, pcap epoch seconds) is later than the apply instant. The apply instant in epoch terms is taken from the events.log utc field, which has 1 s resolution; the pcap epoch clock and the host monotonic clock are NOT assumed comparable and no duration is computed across them.
detector_decision.ambiguity_rule: If a run's only detection_trigger has a packet_ts within +/- 1 s of the apply instant's recorded utc second, the run is recorded UNKNOWN with reason trigger_timing_unresolvable.
detector_decision.no_trigger: A run with no qualifying detection_trigger is recorded as NO_TRIGGER, which is a definite outcome, not UNKNOWN.

analysis.primary: 2x2 agreement between the receiver measurement label and the detector decision, over all runs with a definite label and a definite detector outcome
report: sensitivity and specificity with Wilson 95 percent intervals, where sensitivity is the trigger rate among ABOVE_BOUNDARY runs and specificity the no-trigger rate among BELOW_BOUNDARY runs
per-condition detector trigger rate and per-condition above-boundary rate
every UNKNOWN run with its reason
the first-valid-window dispersion of every run, including UNKNOWN runs where one exists
the number of valid windows found per run
analysis.terminology: Runs triggering without an above-boundary measurement are reported as trigger-without-above-boundary, and above-boundary runs without a trigger as missed-above-boundary. Neither is called a false positive or a miss with respect to harm, because harm is not measured here.
analysis.no_retuning: No threshold, condition, statistic, label rule, ordering or exclusion may change after the first S15 run. If the result is poor, it is reported as poor.

prespecified_interpretation.both_point_estimates_at_least_0.8_AND_bo: the detector's run-level decision agrees with the receiver-side dispersion boundary across the sweep in this testbed
prespecified_interpretation.both_point_estimates_at_least_0.8_but_a_: NOT ESTABLISHED at this sample size. An interval-width result, not a disagreement result: the data are consistent with agreement and with substantially worse performance. It must not be reported as agreement. Both point estimates and both class sizes are quoted in the output.
prespecified_interpretation.sensitivity_at_least_0.8_and_specificity: the detector triggers at jitter levels the receiver measurement places below the boundary; report the levels where they diverge
prespecified_interpretation.sensitivity_below_0.8_and_specificity_at: the detector fails to trigger on above-boundary runs; report the levels where it fails
prespecified_interpretation.both_below_0.8_and_overall_agreement_at_: the detector decision is not shown to track the receiver-side measurement; both rates are quoted
prespecified_interpretation.both_below_0.8_but_overall_agreement_abo: neither rate reaches the pre-specified 0.8; both point estimates and both rates are quoted
prespecified_interpretation.only_one_receiver_label_class_produced: sensitivity or specificity is undefined and agreement cannot be assessed
prespecified_interpretation.most_runs_UNKNOWN: the measurement plan failed; report it as a failed validation attempt and do not substitute another label source
prespecified_interpretation.achievability_note: A Wilson 95 percent lower bound above 0.5 needs roughly seven or more runs in a class at a perfect rate. With 30 planned runs the criterion is reachable if both label classes are reasonably populated; if the sweep produces a lopsided split it will not be, and that is reported as the interval-width branch rather than worked around.
prespecified_interpretation.verification: Every branch above was exercised on synthetic inputs before the freeze, including the three UNKNOWN reasons (insufficient valid windows, receiver entered MASTER, trigger timing unresolvable).

smoke_test.requirement: Exactly one isolated smoke run is executed before the batch, into a directory outside s15_runs, and is excluded from all S15 estimation.
checks: every written ptp4l config sets free_running 1
run environment records that host clock adjustment is disabled
detector lifetime bound covers the declared observation period (detector_max_seconds >= settle + impair)
detector observed the whole impaired phase and exited on stream close, not on its watchdog
the apply instant was recorded as a bracketed interval, not a single coarse timestamp
at least two summary windows lie wholly inside the declared impaired phase
run is sealed and every manifest hash verifies
smoke_test.on_failure: Fix and repeat the smoke test. The batch does not start until a smoke run passes. Failed smoke runs are preserved.
smoke_test.runner: run_s15_smoke.sh writes to s15_smoke/<UTC stamp>/ and then runs check_s15_smoke.py, which exits non-zero if any check fails.
smoke_test.exclusion_mechanism: Structural, not procedural: evaluate_s15.py reads only s15_runs/, and the smoke run is written to s15_smoke/. The smoke run cannot enter S15 estimation even by mistake.

failure_and_exclusion_handling: Preserve every attempt including failures. Never delete or rename a run directory. A trial that dies is retained with its reason and counted as UNKNOWN.
why_v3_exists: DETECTOR LIFETIME. run_s15_validation_trial.sh passed --max-seconds 70 to the live detector while SETTLE was 12 s and IMPAIR 80 s. The detector would have exited about 24 s before the impaired phase ended, truncating observation coverage and leaving the capture FIFO without a reader, which also breaks the graceful drain-and-seal. The lifetime is now derived as DET_SETUP_MARGIN + SETTLE + IMPAIR + DET_DRAIN_MARGIN = 20 + 12 + 80 + 60 = 172 s, a bounded watchdog rather than a schedule: the detector normally exits when the sealer closes the FIFO.

TIMING PRECISION. The runner recorded phase times from /proc/uptime formatted to two decimals. That is CLOCK_BOOTTIME at 10 ms resolution, while the evaluator applied a 1 ms exclusion band. The 0.93 ms anchor agreement was measured between ptp4l's log clock and the DETECTOR's CLOCK_MONOTONIC, not against these coarser runner timestamps, so it never licensed a 1 ms band on them. The runner now reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC directly at microsecond precision, the same clock linuxptp print.c reads, and brackets the impairment command with a before and an after timestamp so the apply instant is a measured interval. The fixed 1 ms band is deleted.
WINDOW CONTAINMENT. Eligibility now requires a summary window to lie WHOLLY inside the declared impaired phase, verified against phase2_end_recorded as well as the apply upper bound.

measurement_provenance_verified.source: linuxptp git tag v3.1.1, the version recorded in every run_environment.txt (linuxptp=3.1.1)
measurement_provenance_verified.log_clock: print.c line 68: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts); printed as "%lld.%03ld" using ts.tv_nsec / 1000000, i.e. TRUNCATED to 1 ms. A logged time L means a true time in [L, L + 0.001).
measurement_provenance_verified.summary_print: clock.c clock_stats_update(): stats_add_value on offset and freq, then print only once stats_get_num_values(offset) >= stats.max_count. clock_stats_display() then calls stats_reset on offset, freq AND delay, so a printed summary aggregates exactly (previous summary, this summary].
measurement_provenance_verified.delay_accumulation: clock.c clock_path_delay() line 1626: stats_add_value(c->stats.delay, path_delay) on every path-delay update, i.e. once per Delay_Resp. With logMinDelayReqInterval -3 that is 8 samples per second, about 128 samples per 16 s window. The printed `delay <mean> +/- <dispersion>` is the mean and standard deviation of those samples.
measurement_provenance_verified.cadence_derivation: Under free_running 1, clock_update_slave returns via clock_no_adjust() before the servo path. clock_no_adjust() calls clock_stats_update only once every fest.max_count Sync messages, where fest.max_count = 1 << (freq_est_interval - logSyncInterval) = 1 << (1 - (-3)) = 16 Syncs = 2 s at logSyncInterval -3. stats.max_count = 1 << (summary_interval - logSyncInterval) = 1 << (0 + 3) = 8 offset samples. A summary therefore prints every 8 x 2 s = 16 s EXACTLY, by construction and not by observation. The measured S14 cadence of 16.021 s agrees.
measurement_provenance_verified.consequence: An 80 s impaired phase contains five summary prints, of which four lie wholly inside the phase after the window straddling the apply instant is discarded. The two-window minimum has a margin of two.

execution_instructions.entry_point: bash run_s15_complete.sh, as root, from this directory. It is the only command needed.
execution_instructions.file_creation: The run CREATES files: run directories, logs, captures, manifests, the evaluation JSON, the CSV package and the workbook. That is intended. What is forbidden is editing, tuning or deleting protocol files, scripts, or recorded evidence.
execution_instructions.never_edit_while_running: No file in this directory may be edited while the batch is executing. Bash reads a script by byte offset as it runs; rewriting one in place destroys the running trial. That is exactly how the previous batch was lost.
execution_instructions.interruption: Re-run the same command. Sealed trials are skipped. An unsealed trial stops the run for a human decision and is never overwritten.
execution_instructions.failures: Preserve every failure. No tuning, no selective reruns, no deletion of a failed run.

why_v4_exists: PRE-SPECIFIED BRANCH WORDING. The v3 evaluator's fall-through branch reported 'neither sensitivity nor specificity reaches the pre-specified 0.8' in a case where BOTH point estimates did reach 0.8 and only the interval lower bounds failed. Found by exercising the evaluator on synthetic inputs covering every branch. At the planned sample size a wide interval is the LIKELY outcome, so this branch would probably have been the one that fired, and it would have stated something false about the result. Branch selection is now exhaustive and each message is true of the numbers that selected it; the interval-width case is reported as NOT ESTABLISHED with both point estimates and both sample sizes quoted.

APPLY BRACKET WIDTH. v3 bracketed the tc command with two shell calls to a python one-liner. Each call costs about 18 ms on this host, measured, so the recorded apply interval was roughly 20 ms wide and consisted almost entirely of measurement overhead rather than uncertainty about when the qdisc changed. That is not conservatism, it is a mis-attribution that widens the eligibility exclusion for no reason. Both timestamps are now taken inside apply_impairment.py, around the tc call itself; the observed bracket is sub-millisecond.

SAMPLER CLOCK LOAD. The per-second pmc port-state sampler also called the precise timestamp helper, adding an 18 ms python spawn to every second of a timing-sensitive run. No evaluator reads that log, so it now uses a cheap coarse clock, explicitly labelled and never compared to a ptp4l time.
relationship_to_the_aborted_batch: The aborted batch produced one smoke run and seven clean trials before the trial runner was edited in place while bash was executing it, destroying trial j200_r2 and stopping the loop at 8 of 30. That data is preserved in full under s15_aborted_20260913T182252Z/ and is EXCLUDED from this batch: it is not pooled, not used to tune anything, and not reported as a result. It was never evaluated. Exclusion is structural: evaluate_s15.py reads only s15_runs/, and the archive is not at that path.
why_v5_exists: v5 is v4's content re-issued with authority. v4 held three corrections that were never in force because it was written on the false premise that no run existed.

APPLY BRACKET. Both bracket timestamps are now taken inside apply_impairment.py around the tc call. The aborted batch recorded brackets of 57-88 ms, which was almost entirely the cost of two python spawns rather than uncertainty about when the qdisc changed.

BRANCH WORDING. A pre-specified interpretation branch would have reported 'neither sensitivity nor specificity reaches 0.8' in the case where both point estimates DO reach 0.8 and only the interval lower bounds fail. At this sample size that is the likely outcome. It now reports NOT ESTABLISHED as an interval-width result, quoting both estimates and both class sizes.
SAMPLER CLOCK. The per-second pmc sampler no longer spawns a python interpreter every second of a timing-sensitive run; it uses a coarse clock that no evaluator reads.

RESUME SAFETY. The batch skips a trial that is already present and sealed, and stops on a trial that is present but unsealed rather than overwriting it. An interrupted batch can be restarted without re-running finished trials and without silently replacing a damaged one.
SINGLE ENTRY POINT. run_s15_complete.sh runs preflight, hash verification, smoke, batch, evaluation and the dataset rebuild as hard gates, so no stage can run on the output of a failed one.
